newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says product mix pressured margins.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says product mix pressured margins.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Friday its gross margins would be squeezed as its product mix was becoming more geared toward mobile phones.
Mobile phones have lower margins than the average for group products.
"We rather see price pressure than pressure on margins but apparently some products have been hit," spokesman Per Bengtsson told a news conference.
"The product mix also plays a part. Mobile phones and terminals have in general lower margins than other products."
Ericsson earlier posted a 30 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 2.02 billion crowns.
But the product mix does not account for all of the pressure on margins, Bengtsson added.
"The pressure on margins mainly stems from the mix, but unfortunately you cannot say that it solely derives from the mix," Bengtsson said. "Price pressure is also an explanation."
Regarding the mix of analogue and digital mobile phones, there was an even stronger focus on digital phones in the first quarter, he said.
"Last year 80 percent (of phones) were digital, the rest analogue," Bengtsson said. "During the first quarter the share of digital phones was clearly higher than 80 percent."
